summary: Isomer's CoreTransferable is the `Transferable` protocol as SwiftUI's pickers and drops take it: a type whose values a picker or a drop hands over, `Data` (the bytes) and `URL` (where they are), with `String`. Isomer's SwiftUI re-exports it, as Apple's does. On Apple platforms an app uses Apple's CoreTransferable.
deviations: `Transferable` has no requirements here: the hosts hand over files, and `PhotosPickerItem.loadTransferable(type:)` and `.dropDestination(for:)` read them as `Data` or `URL`. A type of an app's own (with its `transferRepresentation`) is not loaded through it yet.

groups.title: Transfer representations
groups.why: How a type of an app's own says what it can be transferred as (`transferRepresentation`, `DataRepresentation`, `FileRepresentation`, `ProxyRepresentation`, `CodableRepresentation` and their builder), and the standard types' own representations. The hosts' pickers and drops hand over files; reading one as an app's type through its representation is the next step, for drag and drop between views and to other apps.

groups.title: NSItemProvider
groups.why: `NSItemProvider` is an Objective-C class of Foundation's (drag and drop, sharing on Apple platforms); Isomer's Foundation has no Objective-C classes.

additions: Isomer's CoreTransferable declares nothing Apple's lacks; anything listed here is a regression.
